questions.q:
Match the physical quantities given in List-I with dimensions expressed in terms of mass (M), length (L), time (T) and electric current (A) given in List-II.
List-I
(a) Torque
(b) Gravitational constant
(c) Capacitance
(d) Planck's constant
List-II
(i) $[M^{-1}L^{-2}T^4A^2]$
(ii) $[M^1L^2T^{-1}]$
(iii) $[M^{-1}L^3T^{-2}]$
(iv) $[M^1L^2T^{-2}]$
Codes:
options: a - iv, b - ii, c - iii, d - i
a - iv, b - iii, c - i, d - ii
a - iv, b - i, c - iii, d - ii
a - ii, b - i, c - iii, d - iv
questions.explanation: Torque has dimensions $[ML^2T^{-2}]$ (iv); gravitational constant has $[M^{-1}L^3T^{-2}]$ (iii); capacitance has $[M^{-1}L^{-2}T^4A^2]$ (i); Planck's constant has $[ML^2T^{-1}]$ (ii). So a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii.

questions.q: Which of the following expressions can be deduced on the basis of dimensional analysis? (All symbols have their usual meanings)
questions.explanation: Dimensional analysis can only give relations that are products of powers of quantities (with a dimensionless constant), like Stokes' law $F=6\pi\eta rv$; it cannot fix additive terms, or trigonometric/exponential dependence as in the other options. KEA's revised key marked this a grace-mark question, but $F=6\pi\eta rv$ remains the correct choice.

questions.q: Dimensional formula for activity of a radioactive substance is
questions.explanation: Activity is the number of decays per unit time, so its dimensional formula is $M^0L^0T^{-1}$.

questions.q: The true length of a wire is 3.678 cm. When the length of this wire is measured using instrument A, the length of the wire is 3.5 cm. When the length of the wire is measured using instrument B, it is found to have length 3.38 cm. Then the
options: measurement with A is more accurate while measurement with B is more precise.
measurement with B is more accurate and precise.
measurement with A is more precise while measurement with B is more accurate.
measurement with A is more accurate and precise.
questions.explanation: A's reading (3.5 cm) is closer to the true value 3.678 cm, so A is more accurate; B's reading has more decimal places (finer resolution), so B is more precise.

questions.q: The Vernier scale of a travelling microscope has 50 divisions which coincides with 49 main scale divisions. If each main scale division is 0.5 mm, then the least count of the microscope is
questions.explanation: 1 VSD $=\dfrac{49}{50}\times0.5$ mm; least count $=1$ MSD $-$ 1 VSD $=0.5\,\text{mm}\times\dfrac{1}{50}=0.01$ mm.

questions.q: A cylindrical wire has a mass $(0.3\pm0.003)$ g, radius $(0.5\pm0.005)$ mm and length $(6\pm0.06)$ cm. The maximum percentage error in the measurement of its density is
If P, Q and R are physical quantities having different dimensions, which of the following combinations can never be a meaningful quantity ?
questions.explanation: Since P and Q have different dimensions, the subtraction (P $-$ Q) is itself dimensionally meaningless, making option A never meaningful regardless of R.

questions.q: The dimensions of the ratio of magnetic flux ($\phi$) and permeability ($\mu$) are
The resistance R = V/I where V = (100 ± 5) V and I = (10 ± 0.2) A. The percentage error in R is
questions.explanation: Percentage error in R = percentage error in V + percentage error in I = 5% + 2% = 7%.

questions.q: A substance of mass 49.53 g occupies 1.5 cm$^3$ of volume. The density of the substance (in g cm$^{-3}$) with correct number of significant figures is
questions.explanation: As printed, 49.53 g / 1.5 cm$^3$ \approx 33.02 g cm$^{-3}$, which matches none of the options — the data is inconsistent (the volume was likely meant to be 15.00 cm$^3$, giving 3.302 with 4 significant figures). Because of this error KEA awarded grace marks to everyone.

questions.q: The ratio of the dimensions of Planck constant and that of moment of inertia has the dimensions of
questions.explanation: Planck's constant has dimensions of angular momentum (J\,s = kg\,m$^2$/s); dividing by moment of inertia (kg\,m$^2$) leaves dimensions of s$^{-1}$, i.e. frequency.

questions.q: A physical quantity Q is found to depend on observables x, y and z, obeying relation Q = $\dfrac{x^3y^2}{z}$. The percentage error in the measurements of x, y and z are 1\%, 2\% and 4\% respectively. What is percentage error in the quantity Q?
Which one of the following is NOT correct ?
options: Dimensional formula of thermal conductivity (K) is M$^1$L$^1$T$^{-3}$K$^{-1}$
Dimensional formula of potential (V) is M$^1$L$^2$T$^3$A$^{-1}$
Dimensional formula of permeability of free space ($\mu_0$) is M$^1$L$^1$T$^{-2}$A$^{-2}$
Dimensional formula of RC is M$^0$L$^0$T$^{-1}$
questions.explanation: Potential actually has dimension M$^1$L$^2$T$^{-3}$A$^{-1}$ (T exponent should be $-3$, not $+3$), and RC (a time constant) has dimension T$^1$, not T$^{-1}$; so both (2) and (4) are not correct, matching the KEA key.

questions.q: The dimensional formula of a physical quantity is M$^a$L$^b$T$^c$. Then that physical quantity is
options: surface tension if a = 1, b = 1, c = -2
angular frequency if a = 0, b = 0, c = -1
spring constant if a = 1, b = -1, c = -2
questions.explanation: Angular frequency has SI unit s$^{-1}$, i.e. dimensions M$^0$L$^0$T$^{-1}$, so a = 0, b = 0, c = -1.

questions.q: If $C$ be the capacitance and $V$ be the electric potential, then the dimensional formula of $CV^2$ is .................
questions.explanation: $CV^2 = (Q/V)V^2 = QV$, which is energy $= ML^2T^{-2}$; since $A$ does not appear, the formula is $M^1L^2T^{-2}A^0$.

questions.q: The dimensions of 'resistance' are same as those of ......... where $h$ is the Planck's constant, $e$ is the charge.
questions.explanation: Resistance $R=V/I$; dimensional analysis using $E=h\nu$ and charge $e$ shows $[R]$ matches $h/e^2$ (the von Klitzing constant has units of resistance).

questions.q: The number of significant figures in the numbers $4.8000 \times 10^4$ and $48000.50$ are respectively
questions.explanation: $4.8000\times10^4$ has 5 significant figures; $48000.50$ has 7 (all digits count since the decimal point fixes the trailing zeros as significant).
